links.outcome: Comparing complex multiparameter ML models against simple pauci-parameter models on the same data: performance, net benefit, time, carbon
links.effect: Multiparameter models showed superior performance but not consistently better clinical utility; MULTI-PRE needed 100-fold longer inference and 10-fold higher carbon emissions with near-identical net benefit (0.06 vs 0.05).
links.quote: The best-performing multiparameter model (MULTI-PRE) required 100-fold longer inference time and 10-fold higher carbon emissions per prediction versus simple models, while net clinical benefit was nearly identical (0.06 vs 0.05).

unlisted_practices: Measuring carbon footprint and computational efficiency of AI models as a deployment criterion
Preferring simpler resource-efficient models for resource-limited settings

screen.reason: The study conducts an external validation of multiple machine learning models for traumatic brain injury outcome prediction, assessing performance, computational efficiency, and carbon footprint, but does not evaluate a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
